USER: Hi, I need help completing my enrollment for the fall semester.
ASSISTANT: Good morning! I'm Maria from State University Enrollment Services. I'll help you with your fall enrollment. May I have your student ID?
USER: It's SU-20240847.
ASSISTANT: Thank you. I see here... Ms. Ashley Rodriguez?
USER: Yes, that's me.
ASSISTANT: Welcome to State University, Ashley! I see you're an incoming freshman majoring in Computer Science.
USER: That's right.
ASSISTANT: Have you completed your math placement exam?
USER: Yes, I took it last week.
ASSISTANT: Great! You scored 87, which places you directly into Calculus I. No remedial math needed.
USER: Oh good! What about English placement?
ASSISTANT: Your SAT scores exempt you from placement testing. You're cleared for English Composition 101.
USER: Perfect. So what courses should I take first semester?
ASSISTANT: For Computer Science majors, we recommend: Calculus I, Introduction to Computer Science, English Composition, and one general education course.
USER: How many credits is that?
ASSISTANT: Calculus I is 4 credits, Intro to CS is 4 credits, English is 3 credits. With a 3-credit gen ed, that's 14 credits.

conversation_id=college_enroll_001
timestamp=2024-07-15 10:00:00
rounds=7-14
metadata={"business": "State University Admissions", "department": "Enrollment Services", "call_duration": "61 minutes"}
USER: Perfect. So what courses should I take first semester?
ASSISTANT: For Computer Science majors, we recommend: Calculus I, Introduction to Computer Science, English Composition, and one general education course.
USER: How many credits is that?
ASSISTANT: Calculus I is 4 credits, Intro to CS is 4 credits, English is 3 credits. With a 3-credit gen ed, that's 14 credits.
USER: Should I take more?
ASSISTANT: First semester, we recommend 14-16 credits while you adjust to college. You could add another 3-credit course.
USER: What gen ed options do I have?
ASSISTANT: You need humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. Any preference?
USER: I'm interested in psychology.
ASSISTANT: Perfect! Psychology 101 fulfills social sciences. Professor Williams teaches MWF at 10 AM or Professor Chen teaches Tuesday/Thursday at 2 PM.
USER: I'm more of a morning person. Let's do MWF at 10.
ASSISTANT: Added Psychology 101 with Professor Williams, section 03, MWF 10:00-10:50 AM.
USER: What about the Calc class?
ASSISTANT: Calculus I has several options. Professor Johnson has MWF 8:00-9:15 AM, or Professor Kumar has MWF 1:00-2:15 PM.
USER: 8 AM is early but I'll take it. Better to get it done.
ASSISTANT: Registered for MAT-151 Calculus I, section 01, with Professor Johnson, MWF 8:00-9:15 AM, plus Thursday recitation.

timestamp=2024-07-15 10:00:00
rounds=13-20
metadata={"business": "State University Admissions", "department": "Enrollment Services", "call_duration": "61 minutes"}
USER: What about the Calc class?
ASSISTANT: Calculus I has several options. Professor Johnson has MWF 8:00-9:15 AM, or Professor Kumar has MWF 1:00-2:15 PM.
USER: 8 AM is early but I'll take it. Better to get it done.
ASSISTANT: Registered for MAT-151 Calculus I, section 01, with Professor Johnson, MWF 8:00-9:15 AM, plus Thursday recitation.
USER: Recitation?
ASSISTANT: A smaller problem-solving session with a TA. Thursday sections are at 3:00 PM or 5:00 PM.
USER: 3 PM works better.
ASSISTANT: Added Thursday 3:00-3:50 PM recitation, section R04.
USER: Now the Computer Science course?
ASSISTANT: CS-101 Introduction to Computer Science. Professor Martinez teaches Tuesday/Thursday 9:30-10:45 AM with a 2-hour lab.
USER: When are the labs?
ASSISTANT: Lab options are Wednesday 2:00-4:00 PM or Friday 3:00-5:00 PM.
USER: Wednesday at 2 PM is good.
ASSISTANT: Registered for CS-101, section 02, T/Th 9:30-10:45 AM, with Wednesday 2:00-4:00 PM lab, section L03.
USER: And English?
ASSISTANT: English 101 has many sections. There's T/Th 11:00 AM, MWF 2:00 PM, or T/Th 3:30 PM.

conversation_id=college_enroll_001
timestamp=2024-07-15 10:00:00
rounds=19-26
metadata={"business": "State University Admissions", "department": "Enrollment Services", "call_duration": "61 minutes"}
USER: Wednesday at 2 PM is good.
ASSISTANT: Registered for CS-101, section 02, T/Th 9:30-10:45 AM, with Wednesday 2:00-4:00 PM lab, section L03.
USER: And English?
ASSISTANT: English 101 has many sections. There's T/Th 11:00 AM, MWF 2:00 PM, or T/Th 3:30 PM.
USER: T/Th at 11 would work well after my CS class.
ASSISTANT: Perfect. ENG-101 with Professor Thompson, section 07, Tuesday/Thursday 11:00 AM-12:15 PM.
USER: Should I add one more class to get to 15 or 16 credits?
ASSISTANT: You could add a 1-credit freshman seminar or a 3-credit elective. What interests you?
USER: What's the freshman seminar about?
ASSISTANT: FYE-100 'First Year Experience' - study skills, campus resources, career planning. Meets once weekly.
USER: That sounds helpful. When does it meet?
ASSISTANT: Mondays 3:00-3:50 PM or Wednesdays 12:00-12:50 PM.
USER: Mondays at 3 PM works.
ASSISTANT: Added FYE-100, section 12, Mondays 3:00-3:50 PM with advisor Mr. Davis. That brings you to 15 credits.
USER: Perfect. Now what about housing? I applied for campus dorms.
ASSISTANT: Let me check... You're assigned to Lincoln Hall, Room 347, with roommate Jennifer Kim.

conversation_id=college_enroll_001
timestamp=2024-07-15 10:00:00
rounds=25-32
metadata={"business": "State University Admissions", "department": "Enrollment Services", "call_duration": "61 minutes"}
USER: Mondays at 3 PM works.
ASSISTANT: Added FYE-100, section 12, Mondays 3:00-3:50 PM with advisor Mr. Davis. That brings you to 15 credits.
USER: Perfect. Now what about housing? I applied for campus dorms.
ASSISTANT: Let me check... You're assigned to Lincoln Hall, Room 347, with roommate Jennifer Kim.
USER: Is that a double or triple?
ASSISTANT: It's a double room. Lincoln Hall has suite-style rooms - two doubles sharing a bathroom.
USER: So four people share one bathroom?
ASSISTANT: Correct. Your suitemates in room 345 are Emma Wilson and Sarah Chen.
USER: What floor is that?
ASSISTANT: Third floor. Lincoln Hall has elevators and is co-ed by floor - third floor is all female.
USER: Good. What about meal plans?
ASSISTANT: Freshmen must choose from three plans: Unlimited at $2,850/semester, 14 meals/week at $2,450, or 10 meals/week at $2,150.
USER: What's the difference?
ASSISTANT: Unlimited includes all dining halls anytime. The others include that many meal swipes plus $200 dining dollars for cafés.
USER: I'll probably eat breakfast in my room. Let's do 14 meals.
ASSISTANT: Good choice. That's lunch and dinner daily with flexibility. Selected 14-meal plan at $2,450.

timestamp=2024-07-15 10:00:00
rounds=31-38
metadata={"business": "State University Admissions", "department": "Enrollment Services", "call_duration": "61 minutes"}
USER: What's the difference?
ASSISTANT: Unlimited includes all dining halls anytime. The others include that many meal swipes plus $200 dining dollars for cafés.
USER: I'll probably eat breakfast in my room. Let's do 14 meals.
ASSISTANT: Good choice. That's lunch and dinner daily with flexibility. Selected 14-meal plan at $2,450.
USER: Now about tuition - what do I owe?
ASSISTANT: In-state tuition is $6,840 per semester for 12-18 credits. You're at 15 credits, so that's the flat rate.
USER: Plus fees?
ASSISTANT: Student fees are $782, technology fee $145, health services $210. Total fees: $1,137.
USER: So tuition and fees together?
ASSISTANT: $7,977 per semester.
USER: Plus housing and meals?
ASSISTANT: Lincoln Hall is $3,925 per semester. With the meal plan, housing and dining totals $6,375.
USER: So my total semester bill is?
ASSISTANT: $14,352 for fall semester.
USER: I have financial aid. Can you see my package?
ASSISTANT: Yes, you have: Federal Pell Grant $3,200, State Need Grant $2,500, and Merit Scholarship $4,000 per semester.

USER: So my total semester bill is?
ASSISTANT: $14,352 for fall semester.
USER: I have financial aid. Can you see my package?
ASSISTANT: Yes, you have: Federal Pell Grant $3,200, State Need Grant $2,500, and Merit Scholarship $4,000 per semester.
USER: That's $9,700 in aid?
ASSISTANT: Correct. That leaves $4,652 due for fall semester.
USER: Can I do a payment plan?
ASSISTANT: Yes, we offer a 5-month plan. August through December at $930.40 per month, no interest.
USER: When's the first payment?
ASSISTANT: August 15th, then the 15th of each month through December.
USER: That's manageable. How do I set that up?
ASSISTANT: I can enroll you now. There's a $35 enrollment fee for the payment plan.
USER: That's fine. Use my checking account?
ASSISTANT: Yes, we can do automatic bank drafts. I'll need your routing and account numbers.
USER: Routing is 121000358, account is 5529847100.
ASSISTANT: Perfect. Payment plan established. You'll receive confirmation via email.

USER: Routing is 121000358, account is 5529847100.
ASSISTANT: Perfect. Payment plan established. You'll receive confirmation via email.
USER: What about books?
ASSISTANT: Average is $200-300 per class. For your five classes, budget about $1,200.
USER: That's a lot! Any way to save?
ASSISTANT: Check our bookstore's rental program, or buy used. Also, some professors use free online resources.
USER: I'll look into rentals. When can I buy books?
ASSISTANT: Book lists are posted August 1st. Classes start August 28th.
USER: When do I move into the dorm?
ASSISTANT: Freshman move-in is August 24th-25th. You're assigned August 24th, 10 AM - 12 PM time slot.
USER: Is there orientation?
ASSISTANT: Yes, mandatory orientation runs August 25th-27th. Includes campus tour, advisor meetings, and social events.
USER: Do parents come to that?
ASSISTANT: There's a separate parent orientation on August 25th from 2-5 PM.

USER: Is there orientation?
ASSISTANT: Yes, mandatory orientation runs August 25th-27th. Includes campus tour, advisor meetings, and social events.
USER: Do parents come to that?
ASSISTANT: There's a separate parent orientation on August 25th from 2-5 PM.
USER: Good, my mom wants to attend. What about parking?
ASSISTANT: Freshmen can purchase parking permits for $450/semester for Lot G, about 10-minute walk to Lincoln Hall.
USER: I won't have a car first semester.
ASSISTANT: That's common. We have good campus shuttle service and the city bus is free with student ID.
USER: Perfect. I think that covers everything!
ASSISTANT: Great! You're all set for fall. Your next steps are attending orientation and buying books. Any other questions?
USER: No, thank you so much for your help, Maria!
ASSISTANT: You're welcome, Ashley! Have a wonderful freshman year at State University!
